answer: Persistent lineage receipts. Each agent inherits an anchor record from its parent containing a hash of the parent’s interaction history. To register, a new identity must submit a lineage chain that any peer can replay; duplicated roots collide and the mirror check flags shared ancestry. An orchard of valid chains is maintained by peers, so a fake branch must fabricate consistent history back to genesis. Cost: every duplicate requires maintaining an independent plausible history, making replication linearly expensive.
